text: The pipeline is live. This lesson builds the first thing Finance actually looks at: a real view, shaped for how they'll use the data, not a raw dump of the underlying table.

refund_events already updates itself every five minutes. Finance doesn't need a second copy of that data — it needs a shaped, readable window onto the same live table. A view is a saved query with no storage of its own. When refund_events gets a new row, the view reflects it on the very next query, automatically, with nothing to refresh.

Finance's real question is how much are we refunding, by subscriber, by week — so this view aggregates up to that grain. Notice refund_event_count sits right alongside the dollar total, and that's deliberate, not an afterthought. It's the same kind of sanity-check number Lesson 13 reaches for later: if that count ever looks higher than it reasonably should, it's visible right here, without digging into the raw table.
Power BI's Finance page also needs a plain weekly total, independent of subscriber, for a single headline card. Same underlying table, same two sanity-check columns, just a coarser grain.

Worth doing now, while the pipeline is simple: preview this view and write down the current totals. That's the baseline you'll come back to when Lesson 13's numbers stop matching. Next lesson builds Support's view on the same shared foundation.
